tldr_label: TL;DR: Rutte vows NATO will defend every inch of Poland ahead of Monday's emergency council, COP31 teeters in a second day of overtime, and Wall Street licks it

tldr_bullets.label: NATO
tldr_bullets.body: In Warsaw, Rutte pledged NATO would defend every inch of Polish territory. An emergency North Atlantic Council meets Monday on the missile incursion. [[TAG:warning:Monday council]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: A Russian ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's hometown, killed two, including a 7-year-old boy, and wounded 60. [[TAG:danger:civilian toll]]

tldr_bullets.label: Climate
tldr_bullets.body: COP31 entered a second day of overtime. A new draft names no fossil fuels, and an EU official warned the summit could end with no deal. [[TAG:warning:on the brink]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 lost 8.6% last week and Nvidia 23%, its worst week since 2008. The VIX closed near 36 heading into a holiday-shortened week. [[TAG:danger:volatility]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Iran held talks with Qatari mediators and insisted the US accept its conditions to reopen Hormuz, while the IRGC claimed new US drone shootdowns. [[TAG:info:stalled]]

sections.title: NATO: Every Inch
sections.summary: Rutte pledges to defend Poland; emergency North Atlantic Council meets Monday

paragraphs.heading: Rutte in Warsaw
paragraphs.body: US News, carrying Reuters, and CP24 reported that Rutte, visiting Warsaw, said NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory after Russian missiles and a drone came down in Poland. Vatican News reported he pledged solidarity. Kyiv Post reported that Supreme Allied Commander Europe Gen. Grynkewich will look for vulnerabilities in NATO's deterrence posture. [[TAG:info:solidarity]]

paragraphs.heading: Monday Council
paragraphs.body: Kyiv Post, Mezha and Censor.net reported that an emergency North Atlantic Council session meets in Brussels on Monday, with Poland bringing concrete proposals. Rapporteur reported Poland will receive strong support. Censor.net reported Warsaw has sought more support for Operation Eastern Sentry. [[TAG:warning:Monday]]

sections.sources: US News, CP24, Vatican News, Kyiv Post, Mezha, Censor.net, Rapporteur

sections.title: Ukraine: Kryvyi Rih Hit
sections.summary: Missile strike on Zelensky's hometown kills two and wounds 60; drone attacks continue

paragraphs.heading: Kryvyi Rih
paragraphs.body: CBC and AP, via ABC27, reported that a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two people, a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, and wounded 60, including six children. Officials said about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged. Russia's Defense Ministry said it hit a thermal power plant. [[TAG:danger:civilians]]

paragraphs.heading: Front and Proposals
paragraphs.body: Kyiv Post, publishing ISW's assessment, reported Russian advances near Kupyansk, Lyman and Dobropillya, and a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. ISW also noted Zelensky's proposal for localized ceasefires to evacuate civilians from 15 occupied settlements along the Dnipro. Ukrinform reported Russia launched 148 drones overnight, 117 of which were downed. Casualty figures from Ukrainian sources could not be independently verified.

sections.title: COP31: On the Brink
sections.summary: Second day of overtime; new draft omits fossil fuels as EU warns of no deal

paragraphs.heading: Sunday Draft
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that COP31 talks entered a second day of overtime as a new draft faced scrutiny, and Gulf News reported that fossil fuels are still missing from the text. Al-Monitor and Yahoo reported the summit president said a final deal was close. Reports said the draft refers to the 2023 agreement on transitioning away from fossil fuels without naming coal, oil or gas. [[TAG:warning:no fossil language]]

paragraphs.heading: Conflicting Accounts
paragraphs.body: An EU official reportedly called the text backwards and warned of a real possibility of no deal. Observers said Saudi Arabia and other producers pushed to keep fossil fuels out and carbon removal in. Headtopics reported a final deal had been reached, but Reuters-based accounts said approval was still pending, so adoption is unconfirmed. OnlineKhabar reported agreement on a two-year programme on mountains and climate change. [[TAG:info:unconfirmed]]

sections.title: Markets: After the Rout
sections.summary: S&P 500 lost 8.6% on the week and Nvidia 23%; VIX near 36 into a holiday week

paragraphs.heading: The Damage
paragraphs.body: Yahoo Finance reported that the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction on Friday as the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains. Reports put the S&P 500's weekly loss at 8.6% and Nvidia's at 23%, its worst week since October 2008, and Futu's weekend summary called it Nvidia's largest weekly drop in 18 years. Mostly Markets tied Friday's slide to the report of an SEC probe into Nvidia. The VIX closed at 35.89, its highest since April 2025. [[TAG:danger:worst week]]

paragraphs.heading: Week Ahead
paragraphs.body: TipRanks' weekly preview and Cardano Capital pointed to inflation and growth data as the next test of the Fed's hawkish stance in a holiday-shortened US week. The Rio Times reported the AI rout also rattled Latin American markets, weakening Brazil's real and Chile's peso. [[TAG:info:data ahead]]

sections.title: Iran: Conditions and Claims
sections.summary: Tehran meets Qatari mediators and repeats its terms; IRGC claims US drone shootdowns

paragraphs.heading: Diplomacy
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Iran held talks with Qatari mediators and urged the US to accept its conditions, which include ending the war and lifting sanctions and the naval blockade, before Hormuz reopens. Iranian officials said the talks are not yet formal negotiations. CBS News reported that Trump wants a permanent deal and suggested his next move may not come until 2027. Khaama reported Araghchi saying sanctions and strikes cannot end the war. [[TAG:info:no talks yet]]

paragraphs.heading: On the Water
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that the IRGC claimed it downed US drones over Hormuz, with no immediate US comment, and that Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire at an industrial facility. ABC News reported the IRGC said its Bahrain attacks targeted US Patriot sites. These claims are unverified. [[TAG:warning:unverified]]

sections.sources: Al Jazeera, CBS News, Khaama, ABC News

sections.title: Israel: Talks and Gaza Strikes
sections.summary: Eisenkot invites Likud to marathon talks; disputed Gaza strike on aid vehicle

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: France 24 and Euronews reported that Eisenkot invited Netanyahu's Likud to marathon coalition talks starting Sunday. ABC Australia and World Today Journal reported he ruled out serving under Netanyahu. JNS reported that Likud has set its own conditions for a unity government. [[TAG:info:talks Sunday]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, Haaretz and US News reported that an Israeli strike on a vehicle distributing food aid killed three. The Jerusalem Post reported the IDF said the occupants were Islamic Jihad operatives, a claim others dispute. The National reported strikes killed nine across Gaza over two days and that a Board of Peace adviser criticized Israel. [[TAG:danger:accounts conflict]]

sections.title: Africa: Two Fronts
sections.summary: Sudan's army gains in West Kordofan; Ethiopia-Eritrea border buildup deepens

paragraphs.heading: Sudan
paragraphs.body: Sudan Tribune and Anadolu reported that Sudan's army and allies seized several areas from the RSF in West Kordofan, and Al Jazeera analyzed how those gains could turn the tide, noting the region's oil fields. A rights monitor cited by Sudan Tribune accused the RSF of killing civilians there. CFR's tracker noted the RSF still controls Darfur. [[TAG:warning:Kordofan]]

paragraphs.heading: Ethiopia and Eritrea
paragraphs.body: US News, carrying Reuters, reported both countries have massed forces along their border, while Eritrea denies any incursion. France 24 reported troops mobilizing along the border. Reuters could not confirm reports of skirmishes. [[TAG:danger:war risk]]
